newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britons to lose Hong Kong visa privileges.
newsitem.headline: Britons to lose Hong Kong visa privileges.

text.p: Britons will no longer be able to step off a flight to Hong Kong and straight into a job beginning in April under a new bill announced on Thursday.
The Hong Kong government said it had drafted legislation rescinding visa privileges for Britons ahead of the colony's return to Chinese rule on July 1.
The bill requires Britons to obtain a work permit, just like any other foreign national.
About 200,000 British nationals live in Hong Kong, out of a population of six million, Immigration Department figures show.

"As the special constitutional relationship between the United Kingdom and Hong Kong will come to an end in a few months, it is time to put an end to the immigration privileges enjoyed by British citizens," Immigration Director Regina Ip told a news conference.
The bill, which is not expected to run into serious opposition, would require British citizens to obtain work permits from April 1.
British tourists will get their 12-month visa-free visitor's stay period slashed in half.
Britons already resident in Hong Kong will not be subject to the new rules until their year-long entitlement expires.

The ranks of British expatriates enjoying luxury housing benefits and generous perks have thinned in recent years, but low-tax Hong Kong has proved a magnet for young Britons who form an army of casual workers, delivering sandwiches, serving beers and teaching English.
Many of them stop off for a few months at a time to replenish their bank balances to backpack around Asia.
"The essense of the proposal is to provide a level playing field for all foreign nationals in Hong Kong," Ip said.
"British citizens will be treated on the same basis as all other foreign nationals. There will be no question of any discrimination against them."
The government will propose the laws to the Legislative Council on Wednesday.
The British Chamber of Commerce called the proposals fair.

"I think the important point to remember is that all we are trying to do is to get British citizens onto the same basis as other foreign nationals," Christopher Hammerbeck, the chamber's executive director said.
